title: The near-linear bound for planar halving lines
decision_reason: Original exact formulation, two independently authored explicit restatements, current theorem-scope review, duplicate check and separated A59 self-pass passed; no material matching resolution conflict located.

problem_fingerprint.objects: For each even integer n>=2, a set P of n distinct points in R^2, with no three collinear.
problem_fingerprint.observable: h(P) counts unordered pairs {p,q} whose complete supporting line leaves exactly (n-2)/2 other points in each open half-plane. h(n) is the maximum over all such P.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: For every real epsilon>0 there exists a finite constant C_epsilon>0 such that h(n)<=C_epsilon n^(1+epsilon) for every even n>=2.
problem_fingerprint.geometry: Actual straight lines in the Euclidean plane; no bound on spread, coordinates or convex layers; no random-input assumption.
problem_fingerprint.normalization: A halving line is counted once, not once per orientation. ELSS73 Definition 4.4 uses e_m=h(2m). Its little-o-for-every-epsilon version and the survey's big-O-for-every-epsilon version are equivalent by replacing epsilon with epsilon/2.
problem_fingerprint.family_policy: One canonical planar counting conjecture; do not count edge, line, dual-middle-level, parity or k-set formulations as additional entries.
problem_fingerprint.application: Point-line duality identifies each halving edge with a middle-level crossing of affine functions. This controls the number of membership changes when retaining the cheapest half of linearly varying costs; it does not bound arbitrary parametric matroid optimization.

second_review.arrangement: Primary-agent research followed by a clearly separated adversarial self-pass; no independent agent or human review.
issues_found: Initial fingerprint placed Definition 4.4 on p.144; visual inspection shows p.145.
Several sources use different halving/bisection orientation conventions or conflate a single epsilon with every epsilon.
A general parametric-matroid lower bound could be mistaken for a uniform-selection obstruction.
The fresh search surfaced an inaccessible July 2026 small-set preprint.
issues_resolved: Corrected the exact original locator after inspecting the printed page; retained e_m=h(2m).
Retained through-two-points definition, arbitrary real coordinates and all-epsilon quantifier.
Read Dey Section 4.1 and confined the application to unconstrained cheapest-half selection.
Recorded metadata-only access separately; did not assert or use its uninspected theorems. No complete-resolution claim was present in the available title/abstract.
second_review.application_check: N08 p.3 identifies halving edges with middle-level vertices. A swap between ranks n/2 and n/2+1 changes the optimal cheapest-half subset. This is an explanatory inference, not a claimed runtime theorem.
second_review.search_limit: Relevant statements and proof portions were checked; no independent proof certification or reproduction of coordinate computations.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: The historical n log n expectation is surpassed by a subpower exponential factor.
resolution_comparisons.assessment: This disproves an O(n log n) reading, while exp(c sqrt(log n))/sqrt(log n)=o(n^epsilon) for every fixed epsilon>0. The precise near-linear clause survives.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: General point sets, at most 6.48 n(k+2)^(1/3) (k+1)-sets.
resolution_comparisons.assessment: Putting k near n/2 retains exponent 4/3, above 1+epsilon for epsilon<1/3.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Even n>=282, bound by the largest real root a_n; a_n-(29/8)^(1/3)n(n-1)^(1/3)=-29n/6+o(n).
resolution_comparisons.assessment: A linear subtraction leaves the 4/3 exponent unchanged.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Odd-cardinality recurrences and finite improvements for 35,59,95,97 points; h(n)>=(3n-1)h(n+1)/(2n+2).
resolution_comparisons.assessment: These are lower-bound transfers and finite examples, with no polynomial-exponent lower bound contradicting the target and no matching universal upper bound.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Cumulative levels k<=1 in dimension n-3; nonpointed coneighborly spherical configurations can concentrate quadratically many vertices at central levels.
resolution_comparisons.assessment: Affine planar point sets correspond to pointed rank-three configurations. The full remark explicitly retains their gap; neither the dimensional theorem nor nonpointed examples settle it.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Dense-set lower bounds with subpower exponential factors, including higher-dimensional extensions.
resolution_comparisons.assessment: No contradiction to planar n^(1+epsilon); dense-set upper bounds require a fixed spread assumption absent from the question.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: A matching n k^(1/3) lower bound for general parametric matroids.
resolution_comparisons.assessment: General matroid feasibility is broader than selecting any n/2 options. It cannot be transferred to uniform selection or middle-level complexity without a missing reduction.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Partial settlement of ELSS Conjecture 5.4 about intersecting graph edges, while Remark (4) separately retains Conjecture 5.2.
resolution_comparisons.assessment: Different extremal observable; the adjacent original conjecture number is material.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Linear time to find a single halving edge through a specified point using orientation queries.
resolution_comparisons.assessment: Runtime for finding one witness does not bound the total number of witnesses.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: For each n>=3, some maximizing point set has triangular convex hull.
resolution_comparisons.assessment: Three extreme points leave arbitrarily many interior points; this is not the all-points-in-convex-position case and gives no requested exponent.

independently_authored_corroboration.assessment: Nivasch and Roldán-Pensado–Soberón independently state the same near-linear conjecture. Streltsova–Wagner retain the planar bound gap in 2025. None shares an author with ELSS73. Mirrors and preprint/published versions are not counted separately.

Ratio of optimized network lengths, not the number of balanced separators.
Uniform graph-diameter bound with variable dimension; no middle-level count.

duplicate_check.result: No equivalent active or accepted draft found. Upstream equals local HEAD; connected GitHub returns no open PRs.

normalization_checks: Each geometric line counted once; pair endpoints removed before taking the two equal half-plane counts.
Even n>=2 includes the two-point case. Finitely many initial sizes can be absorbed into C_epsilon.
No uniformity in epsilon is asserted. A single exponent such as 1.001 would not suffice.
ELSS73 e_m=h(2m); big-O and little-o for every positive epsilon are equivalent via epsilon/2.
Actual affine straight lines are distinguished from nonpointed spherical configurations and non-realizable pseudolines.
The application is inferred directly from the verified duality; it counts membership changes in an unconstrained cheapest-half selection problem.
